summary: Ayu Khandro (1839–1953) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies practitioner. She studied under Nyala Pema Dündul, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé, Chokgyur Lingpa, and Drodul Pawo Dorje, and taught A Dzom Gyalsé Gyurmé Dorjé and Namkhai Norbu.
Ayush Maheshwari works in computational fields and Indology. He earned his PhD at the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay and later held a post there.

Ayya Khema (1923–1997) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies teacher. She studied under Phra Khantipalo, Ajahn Singtong, Ajahn Maha Bua, Narada Mahathera, and Matara Sri Nyanarama. She founded Wat Buddha Dhamma and taught at Buddha-Haus from 1989.
Azizah Nur is a PhD student at the Australian National University, attested in 2026, studying under doctoral supervisor Assa Doron.

B. Alan Wallace is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a BA from Amherst College and a PhD from Stanford under Carl Bielefeldt. He taught at Rabten Choeling (1975–1979), UC Santa Barbara (~1997–2001), and founded the Santa Barbara Institute for Consciousness Studies (2003).

B. N. K. Sharma (1909–2005) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied under Satyadhyana Tirtha and at the University of Madras. He served as principal of Rajah's College (1938–1948) and professor of Sanskrit at Ramnarain Ruia College (1953–1969).

Baatr U. Kitinov is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned his PhD at Moscow State University and serves as Associate Professor of World History at Peoples' Friendship University of Russia.

Bahadur Chand Chhabra (1908–1990) was an Indologist and archaeologist who earned his doctorate from Leiden University. He served at the Archaeological Survey of India (1935–1966), as Government Epigraphist (~1949–1953), and as professor at Panjab University (~1965–1973).

Bai Su (1922–2018) was a Chinese archaeologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and sinologist. He completed graduate studies at Peking University under Chengjun Feng, Zuoyun Sun, Rong Geng, and Yongtong Tang, and served as a professor at Peking University (1948–2004).
Baiei Henmi (1891–1977) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Tokyo Imperial University and held a post at Tama Art University.

Baihui Wu (1919–2014) was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Visva-Bharati University (~1946–1951), Peking University as Professor of Sanskrit, and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences and Institute of Philosophy (~1978).

Baij Nath Puri (1916–1996) was an Indologist and historian who earned an M.Litt. and D.Phil. at the University of Oxford. He served as Professor and Head of Ancient Indian History and Archaeology at the University of Lucknow (~1971–1976).

Bal Gangadhar Tilak (1856–1920) was an Indology and history scholar who studied at Deccan College and Government Law College, Mumbai. He taught at the New English School (~1880–1885) and served as a mathematics teacher at Fergusson College (~1885–1890).

Bal Krishen Thapar (1921–1995) was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at Punjab and Heidelberg universities and under Mortimer Wheeler. He served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1978–1981) and Chairman of CCRT (1982–1992).
Bala Sahai Shastri was an Indologist who worked at Panjab University, where he was attested as an Assistant in 1932 and as in-charge of the Sanskrit Section in 1941.

Baliram Shukla is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who held positions at Savitribai Phule Pune University, including Head of the Department of Philosophy (attested 2001) and Professor (attested 2026).
Balram Shukla (born 1982) is an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Delhi from ~1999 to 2010 and became a professor there around 2013.

Bangwei Wang (born 1950) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology. He completed his doctoral dissertation at Peking University in 1987 and served there as a professor, attested between 2000 and 2026.

Banikanta Kakati (1894–1952) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Cotton University, Presidency College Kolkata, and the University of Calcutta. He was a professor at Cotton University (1918–1947) and later Dean and department head at Gauhati University (1948).

Bapu Deva Sastri (1821–1900) was an Indology scholar who studied at Sehore Sanskrit School under Lancelot Wilkinson, Dhundhiraja Misra, and Sevarama. He taught at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University from 1842 to 1889.
